forces.title: Second Asset Monetisation Plan to boost private investment.
forces.description: The government's Second Asset Monetisation Plan (NMP) aims to reinvest Rs. 10 lakh crore (US$ 115.34 billion) in capital for new projects between 2025-30. This initiative is designed to recycle capital and significantly attract private sector participation in infrastructure development, creating a strong pipeline for infrastructure investment vehicles like InvITs.

forces.title: Infrastructure Finance Secretariat enhances private investment opportunities.
forces.description: The establishment of the Infrastructure Finance Secretariat is a key governmental initiative to enhance opportunities for private investment in infrastructure. This secretariat is intended to assist all stakeholders, streamlining processes and providing support to attract greater private capital into the sector, directly benefiting infrastructure investment vehicles.

forces.title: NIP expansion provides massive pipeline for infrastructure investment.
forces.description: The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) has significantly expanded, with the number of projects growing to ~14,563 from ~6,800 at inception, and total investment rising by ~92% to Rs. 213 trillion (US$ 2.41 trillion). This massive pipeline across 33 sectors offers abundant opportunities for financing through infrastructure investment vehicles.

forces.title: SEBI broadens SPV definition for InvITs to ensure continuity.
forces.description: SEBI's proposal to broaden the definition of Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) under InvIT Regulations is a welcome structural change. It allows InvITs to continue holding SPVs even after concession expiry or termination, addressing regulatory uncertainty and allowing efficient resolution of statutory/contractual obligations without forced premature sales or settlements.
forces.source_title: SEBI’s new InvIT Playbook: What is the word on the street about the new draft consultation paper?

forces.title: SEBI expands InvITs' liquid mutual fund investment options.
forces.description: SEBI's proposal to allow InvITs to invest in liquid mutual fund schemes with a credit risk value of 10 or above (Class A-I and B-I) expands their eligible investment universe. This change provides InvITs with greater cash-management flexibility and broader investment opportunities for their liquid assets without compromising on conservative risk parameters.
forces.source_title: SEBI’s new InvIT Playbook: What is the word on the street about the new draft consultation paper?

forces.title: Private InvITs now permitted to invest in greenfield projects.
forces.description: SEBI proposes allowing privately listed InvITs to invest up to 10% of their total asset value in greenfield, under-construction projects within their 20% non-core bucket. This aligns private InvITs with public InvITs, fostering new infrastructure creation and potentially attracting institutional capital to projects at earlier stages, thereby expanding the investable universe.
forces.source_title: SEBI’s new InvIT Playbook: What is the word on the street about the new draft consultation paper?

forces.title: SEBI expands InvITs' borrowing uses, allowing capex and refinancing.
forces.description: SEBI proposes amending regulations to allow InvITs with net borrowings exceeding 49% of asset value to raise additional debt for purposes like capital expenditure for performance/capacity enhancement, major maintenance for road projects, and refinancing existing debt. This removes a significant operational constraint, offering greater financial flexibility and improving debt management for InvITs.
forces.source_title: SEBI’s new InvIT Playbook: What is the word on the street about the new draft consultation paper?

forces.title: Government plans risk guarantee fund to boost investor confidence.
forces.description: The government is planning a Rs 20,000 crore (US$ 2.33 billion) risk guarantee fund to support infrastructure investment. This fund aims to cover losses from policy uncertainty and non-commercial risks, thereby boosting investor confidence and attracting more private capital into infrastructure projects, which directly benefits investment vehicles.

forces.title: Low domestic institutional participation limits InvIT market depth.
forces.description: Domestic institutions, including mutual funds, provident/pension funds, banks, and insurers, hold a modest ~7% of InvIT units, contrasting sharply with global investors' 55% stake. This low participation indicates an underpenetrated domestic investor base, limiting market depth and potentially increasing reliance on foreign capital, thus posing a risk to the long-term robustness of the InvIT market.
forces.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

forces.title: InvITs face underpenetrated bond market for debt financing.
forces.description: The borrowing mix of InvITs heavily relies on banks, with term loans constituting nearly two-thirds of total borrowings. Bond issuances account for only about 20% of combined debt, highlighting an underpenetrated capital market base. This structural imbalance suggests that while InvIT platforms mature, they still face limitations in diversifying their debt financing beyond traditional bank loans.
forces.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

forces.title: Road InvIT monetisation challenged by valuations and asset availability.
forces.description: The monetisation of road assets through InvITs faces challenges, including lower valuation multiples for Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) projects due to high leverage and competitive bidding. Additionally, the limited availability of mature toll road assets eligible for primary market monetisation constrains the asset pool, posing a risk to the desired pace and pricing of road InvIT growth.
forces.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

forces.title: Transmission InvIT growth tempered by sponsor credit and refinancing.
forces.description: Despite a large investment opportunity in the transmission sector (Rs 4.86 lakh crore till 2030–31), the prospects for monetising these assets through InvITs are diminished. This is primarily due to the strong credit profiles of existing sponsors and the ample availability of attractively priced refinancing avenues outside of InvIT structures, reducing the incentive for InvIT-based capital.
forces.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

forces.title: Renewable InvITs face PPA delays, technology risks, grid constraints.
forces.description: Renewable energy InvITs face several prominent headwinds, including delays in signing power purchase agreements (PPAs), technological risks associated with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) projects, and constraints on transmission evacuation capacities. These factors can impede the smooth integration and monetisation of renewable assets, affecting the growth trajectory of renewable InvITs.
forces.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

forces.title: Rising costs challenge warehousing InvIT profitability.
forces.description: Warehousing InvITs face near-term challenges from rising land prices and higher construction costs. These factors, relative to rental yields, can compress margins and affect profitability, despite buoyant underlying demand from e-commerce and logistics. This poses a key risk to the financial viability and attractiveness of new warehousing InvIT projects.
forces.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

forces.title: Rising government capex supports infrastructure financing via InvITs.
forces.description: India's infrastructure growth is significantly supported by a rise in capital expenditure, increasing from Rs. 2.63 lakh crore (US$ 40.81 billion) in FY18 to Rs. 11.21 lakh crore (US$ 126.85 billion) in FY26 (BE). This sustained government investment, coupled with expanding financing through vehicles like NBFCs and InvITs/REITs, creates a robust environment for infrastructure investment.

forces.title: Properly structured PPPs critical for unlocking private infrastructure investment.
forces.description: Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) are seen as critical for unlocking private investment and accelerating India’s infrastructure expansion. With nearly 60% of national highways developed between 2009 and 2013 under PPP models, structured partnerships are expected to continue driving infrastructure growth and provide investment opportunities for various financing vehicles.

forces.title: Geopolitical events pose downside risk to state capex and infra monetization.
forces.description: Geopolitical crises, particularly in West Asia, introduce downside risks to state capital expenditure and infrastructure monetization efforts. The impact on energy and commodity prices can exert pressure on state revenues and expenditures, constraining the pace of capital outlay. This also affects investor confidence for Public Private Partnership (PPP) projects, hindering funding for higher capital outlay.
forces.source_title: State Finances: Capex Growth moderates to ~8-10% in FY27

viewpoints.title: InvITs poised for steady growth, supported by robust credit and asset pools.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge expects InvITs to see continued growth in FY26, with an additional Rs 1 lakh crore AUM from roads, warehousing, transmission, and renewable energy sectors. The sector's credit profile is robust due to diversified, operational assets. Stable leverage at 49% in FY26, driven by valuation gains and equity issuances, underscores strong investor confidence. However, deepening the domestic investor base remains a key potential area for growth.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

viewpoints.title: InvIT bond market participation expected to remain moderate despite sector maturity.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge notes that bond market participation for InvITs is likely to stay moderate, constituting only about 20% of the estimated Rs 3.70 lakh crore debt by March 31, 2026. This highlights an underpenetrated capital market base, even as InvIT platforms mature, suggesting a continued reliance on bank financing rather than diversified debt instruments.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

viewpoints.title: Roads segment offers strong InvIT monetisation pipeline, but valuation challenges persist.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge highlights the robust monetisation pipeline within the roads segment for InvITs, driven by operational HAM assets and ambitious targets under NMP-II for FY26-FY30. However, the pace and pricing of road asset monetisation will be influenced by HAM project valuations and the limited availability of mature toll assets, indicating a cautious outlook on optimal deal terms.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

viewpoints.title: Transmission and solar InvITs face growth tempered by refinancing and concession structures.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge identifies long-term potential for transmission and solar assets within InvITs, supported by their stable revenue profiles. However, growth in these sub-sectors is tempered by the long-tenure concession structures and the availability of attractively priced refinancing debt outside of InvITs, which can reduce the incentive for sponsors to monetise assets through InvIT platforms.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

viewpoints.title: Warehousing InvITs well-positioned with healthy occupancy and moderate leverage.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge holds a positive view on warehousing InvITs, noting their strong positioning. This is attributed to healthy occupancy levels driven by buoyant demand from e-commerce, 3PL, and multimodal supply chains, coupled with moderate leverage. These factors contribute to stable cash flows and attractive investment profiles for warehousing infrastructure.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

viewpoints.title: Significant untapped domestic investor base for InvITs, especially mutual funds and retail.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge points out that domestic institutions like mutual funds, provident/pension funds, and insurers hold only about 7% of InvIT units, contrasting sharply with global investors' 55% stake. This low participation indicates an underpenetrated domestic investor base, limiting market depth and potentially increasing reliance on foreign capital, highlighting a strong opportunity for broader domestic engagement.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s InvITs AUM to reach Rs 7.25-7.50 lakh crore by FY26

viewpoints.title: SEBI’s InvIT regulatory proposals expected to enhance operational ease and investor appeal.
viewpoints.description: KPMG views SEBI's draft consultation paper for InvITs as a positive development, offering 'clinical fixes' to reduce operational friction and broaden investible options. The proposals aim to align financing tools with the real-world lifecycle of infrastructure assets without weakening prudential safeguards, thereby strengthening the InvIT platform as an attractive option for developers and investors.
viewpoints.source_title: SEBI’s new InvIT Playbook: What is the word on the street about the new draft consultation paper?

viewpoints.title: Private InvITs could benefit from higher greenfield investment cap for increased infrastructure creation.
viewpoints.description: KPMG notes that SEBI's proposal to allow private InvITs to invest up to 10% of asset value in greenfield projects is positive, creating a level playing field with public InvITs. However, given the higher risk appetite of institutional investors in private InvITs, a higher threshold could have been permitted. This would further augment new infrastructure creation and attract institutional capital at earlier stages of development.
viewpoints.source_title: SEBI’s new InvIT Playbook: What is the word on the street about the new draft consultation paper?

viewpoints.title: Broadening InvIT SPV definition resolves post-concession regulatory uncertainty.
viewpoints.description: KPMG welcomes SEBI's proposal to broaden the definition of Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) under InvIT Regulations. This change allows InvITs to continue holding SPVs even after concession expiry, resolving regulatory uncertainty regarding post-reversion statutory and contractual obligations. It removes pressure for premature settlements or discounted sales of entities with pending disputes, ensuring more efficient asset resolution.
viewpoints.source_title: SEBI’s new InvIT Playbook: What is the word on the street about the new draft consultation paper?
